product: Repligen makes bioprocessing technologies and systems for biologic drug manufacturing across filtration and fluid management, chromatography, process analytics and proteins.
demand: Demand is improving: Q2 2026 organic revenue grew 13% with sustained order momentum, diversified portfolio strength in proteins and analytics, and gains in China and Asia Pacific.
pricing_power: Mixed to moderate: adjusted gross margin is about 54%, and growth has come from volume and mix rather than price, suggesting limited pricing power against larger competitors.
competition: Repligen competes with larger, better-financed bioprocessing players including Cytiva (Danaher), Thermo Fisher, Sartorius and MilliporeSigma, and with cell-processing tool makers in BioLife market.
team: CEO Olivier Loeillot leads after a recent CEO transition. Long-serving board member Karen A. Dawes retires effective 2026-09-30. Jacob Johnson is VP of Investor Relations.
market_strategy: Bolt-on M&A plus organic innovation: the BioLife acquisition is meant to fast-track cell-therapy leadership and add recurring high-margin consumables, while Repligen expands in Asia Pacific and invests in process analytics and AI-enabled tools.
bull: Q2 2026 organic revenue rose 13% with raised FY26 guidance of 10.5-13.5% and adjusted EPS $2.03-$2.09; four dated target raises in 90 days (UBS 195->225 on 2026-09-09); BioLife adds cell-therapy growth with guided accretion.
bear: GAAP net income fell to $5.0M from $14.9M, GAAP operating margin only 6.8%, gross margin slipped 1.8pts, and the $1.5B stock-funded BioLife deal dilutes holders with integration and impairment risk; consensus targets sit below market price.
falsifier: BioLife stockholders fail to approve the merger at the 2026-10-05 special meeting, or Q3 2026 GAAP operating margin stays near 6.8% with no accretion progress.

web_what_changed: On 2026-07-21 Repligen agreed to acquire BioLife Solutions for about $1.5B enterprise value, $11.25 cash plus 0.1442 RGEN shares ($31.00 value per share). Q2 2026 results on 2026-07-28 showed revenue of $204M, up 12% reported and 13% organic, and FY26 organic growth guidance was raised to 10.5%-13.5% with adjusted EPS $2.03-$2.09. HSR waiting period expired 2026-09-03.
web_not_known_yesterday: No company-specific disclosure dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25 was found. The latest primary item read is the 2026-09-15 8-K: director Karen A. Dawes will retire effective 2026-09-30. HSR antitrust clearance (2026-09-03) and the BioLife special meeting date (2026-10-05) were already disclosed on 2026-09-08.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Growth is demand and volume driven, not price: Q2 2026 organic revenue rose 13% on continued order momentum, portfolio diversification and market outperformance, with strength in proteins and process analytics. Mix helped; management did not cite pricing as a growth driver. FX added under 50bps to full-year 2026 revenue guidance.
web_suppliers: Repligen is largely vertically integrated, manufacturing its own bioprocessing consumables and systems; main sites are in the U.S. with additional sites in Estonia, Germany, Ireland, the Netherlands and Sweden. No named key suppliers or supplier constraints were disclosed in the releases and filings read, so specific constraints are not found.
web_customers: Customers are primarily biopharmaceutical drug developers and contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) worldwide. Specific customer names and concentration percentages are not disclosed in the documents read, so concentration is not found. BioLife adds cell-therapy customers; its CryoStor media supports 18 commercially approved therapies.
web_who_loses: Larger bioprocessing rivals in filtration, chromatography and process analytics lose relative share, and cell-therapy biopreservation competitors lose ground, as Repligen bundles BioLife CryoStor media with its own workflow. BioLife loses its separate public listing. Smaller single-product bioprocessing peers are most exposed.
web_contradicting_evidence: GAAP net income fell to $5.0M in Q2 2026 from $14.9M; GAAP diluted EPS dropped to $0.09 from $0.26 and GAAP operating margin was only 6.8%. H1 2026 booked a $13.7M loss on sale of business and the Polymem divestiture is an approximately one-point revenue headwind. The stock-funded deal dilutes holders, and consensus targets ($168.57 to $189.48) sit below the roughly $190 market price.
web_if_management_right: BioLife closes in Q4 2026, adding cell-therapy exposure with more than 20% annual commercial growth, at least $0.05 year-one and $0.25 year-two adjusted EPS accretion, $20M then $30M synergies and more than $300M pro forma cash. Organic growth holds near mid-teens and adjusted operating margin moves toward the high teens.
web_if_management_wrong: If cell-therapy demand or BioLife prove weaker than assumed, integration costs, share dilution and a possible impairment of the roughly $1.5B purchase price hit first. The first visible break is GAAP earnings and margin, already thin, plus missed accretion and synergy targets. The 2026-10-05 BioLife stockholder vote and the 2027-01-31 outside date are the near-term gates.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Cell-therapy CDMOs and developers gaining lower-cost bundled workflow tools; suppliers of biopreservation raw materials, cold-chain logistics and single-use components; and advisors Perella Weinberg, Goldman Sachs and Centerview. Peer bioprocessing names can re-rate on sector capital deployment.
